title: Probe resilience orchestration with traffic slicing and SLO-preservation
creator: Maya Chen
description: Reduce oscillation and unsafe autoscaler handoffs during partial regional failures by orchestrating probe behavior with traffic-slicing policies and multi-tiered readiness levels. Goal: preserve customer-facing SLOs (p99 latency, availability) across regional failover while avoiding autoscaler thrash and large-scale load shedding that impacts high-priority tokens.
background: We observed repeated autoscaler thrashing during region partial degradations when a spike in probe failures caused all replicas to be marked unhealthy simultaneously. Existing probes are single-tier and identical across traffic classes which amplifies noise from transient errors. This ticket defines a coordinated approach: traffic slicing, probe tiering, smoothing windows, and an autoscaler handoff protocol to keep SLOs intact during degradation.
acceptance_criteria: New probe tiers implemented: synthetic, canary, and production readiness with independent windows
Autoscaler no longer flips >1x in a 5-minute window during simulated region failure in canary load test
End-to-end failover test shows p99 latency degradation limited to <20% above baseline and availability stays >= 99.5% for customer-critical tokens
Circuit breaker matrix applied per-region and per-traffic-slice in runtime config and exercised in chaos test
Dashboard shows probe-level signal breakdown, per-slice traffic routing, and rollout status
design_notes: Introduce a probe orchestration layer that schedules probe execution and aggregates results across tiers. Key ideas: 1) Traffic slicing tags requests (priority_token, interactive, background), 2) Synthetic shadow probes that warm instances before routing real traffic, 3) Canary routing with phased increase, 4) Readiness smoothing windows with exponential backoff to avoid synchronized failures.
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Add traffic-slicing header that the routing layer sets and the runtime propagates. Phase 2: Implement probe tiers and a probe scheduler that respects per-slice cadence. Phase 3: Autoscaler integration - expose smoothed readiness score and a 'handoff' flag to prevent instant scale-down of warmed hosts. Phase 4: Circuit breaker config matrix, and rollout behind feature flag.
tradeoffs_and_risks: Pros: better SLO preservation, fewer thrashes, finer-grained control over customer impact. Cons: increased complexity in runtime, potential mismatch between synthetic probes and real request shapes, longer debugging surface. Risk mitigation: start with a small subset of traffic slices and require observational gates before expanding.
test_plan: Unit tests for probe scheduler and smoothing logic. Integration test harness that replays real request traces and injects latency/errors per-region. Chaos test: terminate 30% of hosts in a region while ramping synthetic errors to validate graceful shedding and autoscaler stability. Performance test: ensure probe overhead <1% CPU on hot paths.
qa_steps: Deploy to staging with feature flag enabled for single region and single traffic slice
Run trace-replay load test and validate readiness smoothing behavior in metrics
Execute chaos test (region isolate) and confirm autoscaler backoff prevents thrash
Confirm dashboards surface per-tier probe metrics and alert rules fire only on sustained degradation
monitoring_and_alerting: Add metrics: probe_tier_{synthetic,canary,prod}_failure_rate, readiness_smoother_score, autoscaler_handoff_count, slice_drop_rate. Add alert: readiness_smoother_score < 0.7 for >3m for critical slice => PagerDuty. Add SLO burn rate dashboard for customer-critical tokens.
rollout_plan: Start with internal beta (10% of traffic, critical slice only) for 48h. If stable, expand to 30% with expanded telemetry retention. Final rollout after 7-day observation and signoff from on-call and SRE.
rollout_rollback_criteria: Rollback if autoscaler flip-rate >1/minute sustained for 3 minutes or if p99 latency increases by >50% for critical tokens. Also rollback on any untriaged increase in error budget burn rate.
progress_updates: 2026-02-27: Spike completed to validate traffic-slicing header semantics. Rejected initial header name 'X-Route-Token' in favor of 'X-RW-Traffic-Slice' to reduce collision risk.
2026-03-03: Prototype probe scheduler landed in runtime branch feature/probe-orch. Unit tests added for smoothing window math.
2026-03-07: Integration test with trace replay shows 3x reduction in simultaneous readiness transitions for traced failure pattern. Still tuning canary cadence.
2026-03-10: First canary rollout to internal beta (10% traffic) started. Observability dashboard added and initial metrics look stable for critical token slice.
review_feedback: PM: prefer shorter smoothing windows for interactive slice; suggested 30s base rather than 60s
Design: add explicit synthetic probe shape that mirrors critical token request length distribution
SRE: require a 'graceful handoff' flag in autoscaler API to prevent immediate scale-in on transient failures
